doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: The Freeman family: Von, Bruz, George, and Armstrong lodging with grandparents
summary: He describes his father and uncles as Chicago's premier band, his grandfather the policeman and pianist who hosted Armstrong, Bruz as a Tuskegee Airman, and his grandmother singing gospel.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Wow. Now these guys are pretty modern players too. I guess I had this impression, I have to readjust my thinking, that they were pretty up to date. In other words they were not just playing swing.

No. Well you see my history goes even further back than that. My father, my family, the Freeman family, my father has two brothers. Bruz Freeman and George Freeman. Bruz is a drummer and George is a guitarist. They all played with Charlie Parker. But prior to that, at that time they were the premier band in Chicago. My father is a legend and so are my uncles. But my grandfather is also one, he was one of the first black policemen on the Chicago police force, and my grandmother, my father’s mother and father, Louis Armstrong lived with them when he came up from New Orleans during that period he was in Chicago, where he played with Benny Goodman, you know that whole period when Louis lived in Chicago.
And King Oliver and all those?

Yes. He lived with, when he first came up he stayed with my grandparents. And so my grandfather was also a piano player. And so my dad grew up listening to Louis Armstrong play duets with my grandfather, and my dad and his two brothers of course. My father was actually the first one to become a musician, even though my uncle Bruz was older. He’s the oldest of the three. But he also has another history because he was a Tuskegee Airman. And he also served with Percy Heath. Percy Heath is a Tuskegee Airman. So a lot of history. And then my grandmother was very involved in the church, and she sang in the choir. And she sang with Mahalia Jackson, because her church, which was called the Church of God and Christ, Bishop Ford, who they actually named an expressway in Chicago after him, used to have these things in Sunday church where, in the Gospel world it is a very famous church. Mahalia Jackson sang there, all of the great — God, Clara Ward, all of the great Gospel singers, and my grandmother sang in the choir and sang with these people and played guitar. And that’s what influenced my Uncle George to be a guitarist. So then I grew up in that environment when I was coming up.
